items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: got a chance, like I said, to go on the train into New York City and meet these great jazz musicians with Joe. Jack Teagarden, you name them, you can just name them just like that, off the bat, they were great.

ctx.x: You were taking a stand. That’s interesting. Well I’m interested in how Joe taught you chords and so forth. Did he play a keyboard instrument or did he just talk about it?

No he just talked to me about it and played the clarinet and showed me certain things. I memorized a lot of the stuff that he told me and later on it came out. When I went to the University of California in San Diego and I knew exactly what they were talking about when I was studying music, because I had that instilled in me at an earlier age, about chord progressions and scales and writing and things like that. I knew how to do that way before I was in high school and way before I was in college. Because just by…
Would you do it all over again?
